title: routing-policy-guardian-and-backcompat-adapter
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Replace the brittle ad-hoc routing rule checks with a single, extensible 'Guardian' layer that validates incoming routing DSL/configs, performs semantic checks, and applies a backwards-compatibility adapter (rewriter) so older customer rules continue to work without forcing immediate schema migration.

Scope:
- Design and implement a validation facade (Guardian) that runs early in the config ingestion pipeline. It must perform: schema validation, semantic cross-field checks (region <-> tier coherence, model variant fallbacks), and cost/latency safety heuristics.
- Implement a Backcompat Adapter module that translates legacy rule shapes into the new canonical contract at runtime. The adapter should be configurable: warn-only, autofix, or strict-fail modes.
- Provide a migration CLI (policy-migrate) that can run across a customer’s rule set and emit suggested rewrites with a confidence score.
- Add property-based and fuzz tests for the validator and adapter logic; build a small corpus of customer-inspired fixtures.
- Instrument metrics and rollout gating: counts of rewrites, warnings, failures, and per-organization enforcement state.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Layered enforcement: start with warn-only to avoid customer disruption, then move to autofix where safe, finally strict on a per-org schedule. This reduces incident risk but increases telemetry and rollout complexity.
- Adapter versus migration: implementing an adapter buys time for customers but adds runtime overhead. We will micro-benchmark adapter cost; if cost > 1% p99 latency budget for a route, we will require an offline migration.
- Strict semantic checks (e.g., incompatible region+tier combos) should be configurable per org; default policy is conservative (error on obvious contradictions).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Guardian validates 100% of new inbound rule writes in canary org with warn-only mode enabled.
2) Backcompat Adapter produces idempotent rewrites for at least 95% of legacy patterns in our fixture corpus.
3) CI runs property-based fuzzing with no crashes and reduces known family of misconfigurations by 80%.
4) Metrics and dashboards exposed in Console (per-org enforcement status) and alerts for spikes in rewrites/failures.

Out-of-scope: full UI for rule editing (console UX will be follow-up). Heavy migration assistance (we provide a CLI and suggested rewrites only).

Notes: Implementation will live in policy-engine service; the Guardian will be a single entrypoint that composes small validators to keep code testable and replaceable.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ava Chen: Kickoff sync with product and infra. Agreed on three-phase rollout: warn-only -> autofix -> strict. PM asked for per-org opt-in toggle.

2025-02-18 - Marcus Patel: POC validator implemented (structural checks + tiny semantic rule). Initial perf shows ~0.3ms median overhead on ingest; need p99 check. Added ENG-764322 for perf benchmark tasks.
2025-02-22 - Elena Ruiz (PM): Emphasize migration CLI UX; product wants a dry-run mode and a CSV export of affected rules so SREs can plan cutover windows.
2025-02-27 - Security review (Jake Morris): adapter doesn't introduce new secrets. Recommend review of logging to avoid leaking model IDs in logs. See TODO to redact model_id in telemetry.
2025-03-01 - Design review (Priya Singh): Suggested clearer error codes for semantic failures to map to Console UI. Created label 'error-codes' for follow-up.

2025-03-03 - Marcus Patel: Integrated property-based tests using Hypothesis-style runner. Found a class of rules that produced cyclic fallback references; added a guard to detect cycles and emit a clear diagnostic.

2025-03-05 - Ava Chen: Decided on metrics set: policy.guardian.rewrites, policy.guardian.warnings, policy.guardian.failures, policy.guardian.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99). Added ENG-764323 to wire dashboards.
